title: Fabrication and Deployment of the In Situ Chemotaxis Assay (ISCA)
author: Bennett Lambert
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.398gr9w
materials: UV-sterilise the PDMS slab for 30 minutes together with a clean glass slide (use 80% Ethanol, followed by a ddH2O rinse). 80% Ethanol Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Microscope Slides (102 x 76 mm) Ted Pella Inc. Catalog #260230 00:30:00, UV Treatment

First filter gently (without applying excessive pressure) through a 0.2 μm Sterivex filter. Use 10 mL sterile syringes for filtration (smaller syringes apply too much pressure and compromise the filtration process). Sterivex Filter (0.2 um) Merck Millipore (EMD Millipore) Catalog #SVGPL10RC Syringe (10 mL) Terumo

Finally, filter through a 0.02 μm Whatman filter. It is quite difficult to get water through this last filter, so we recommend carefully assessing the amount of water needed for your experiment before starting the last filtration step. This process, when done properly, ensures complete removal of bacterial cells from seawater and provides a safe medium to resuspend your chemoattractants (it also has the same salinity/density and nutrient content as the bulk seawater surrounding the ISCA, providing an ideal negative control for the assay). Whatman Anotop Filter (0.02 um) Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #WHA68093102

steps.title: Prepare and cast PDMS
steps.instruction: Weigh 26 g of Sylgard 184 PDMS (1:10 curing‑agent:base), degas the mixture under vacuum to remove all bubbles, pour it onto the 3‑D‑printed moulds and cure overnight at 40 °C on a level surface (avoid exceeding 48 °C and limit to ≤6 moulds per batch).

substeps.instruction: Weigh 26 g of PDMS base and curing agent mixed at a 1:10 ratio.
Degas the mixture under vacuum until no bubbles remain.
Pour the degassed PDMS onto the moulds.
Cure at 40 °C overnight on a level surface (max 6 moulds).

steps.title: Cut and release PDMS slab
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, gently cut along the mould edges as close as possible without cutting near the wells, then carefully peel the cured PDMS slab out of the mould without tearing.

steps.title: Trim slab edges
steps.instruction: Trim approximately 1 cm from each side of the PDMS slab with a scalpel, keeping the surface that will be bonded facing up and cutting away from yourself to avoid debris.

steps.title: Clean ISCA ports
steps.instruction: Clear each ISCA port with an 18 G syringe needle sharpened to the port diameter or a 0.8 mm biopsy punch to eliminate obstructions.

steps.title: Remove surface dust
steps.instruction: Wipe the PDMS slab with clean scotch tape to lift dust and debris from the bonding surface.

steps.title: Plasma bond to glass
steps.instruction: Bond the PDMS slab to a glass slide using a plasma oven (BD‑20AC Laboratory Corona Treater) or plasma wand, preferring the oven for uniform covalent bond formation.

steps.title: Post‑bond heat treatment
steps.instruction: Place the glass‑down devices on a hotplate set to 80 °C for ~30 minutes to accelerate covalent bond formation.

steps.title: Protect bonded surface
steps.instruction: Cover the top side of the bonded PDMS slab with clean scotch tape to keep it dust‑free during storage.

steps.title: Assemble flow‑damping enclosure
steps.instruction: Laser‑cut acrylic pieces (McMaster‑Carr), fit them together like a puzzle, fasten with Weld‑On 3 (SCIGRIP) and let the assembly cure overnight.

substeps.instruction: Laser‑cut the acrylic components using the supplied .ai file.
Fit the pieces together in the designed puzzle arrangement.
Apply Weld‑On 3 adhesive to the joints.
Allow the enclosure to cure for ~12 hours (overnight).

steps.title: Pre‑soak enclosure
steps.instruction: After the adhesive has hardened, soak the entire enclosure in deionized water for 24 hours before use.

steps.title: Collect and filter field water
steps.instruction: Collect seawater at the field site into a 50 mL Falcon tube (Fisher Scientific) and filter it through a 0.2 µm Minisart filter (Merck Millipore, catalog #16534K).

steps.title: Prepare chemoattractant solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute chemoattractants in the filtered water to the desired final concentrations; retain the remaining water as negative controls for flow cytometry and sequencing.

steps.title: Load wells with solutions
steps.instruction: Using a 27 G needle (Terumo) attached to a 1 mL sterile syringe, fill each well with the appropriate solution (port facing up), filling slowly until a small droplet emerges from the top surface; use a separate syringe and needle for each solute and avoid trapping air bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Attach a 27 G needle to a sterile 1 mL syringe.
Position the needle in a well with the port facing up.
Inject solution slowly until a droplet appears on the device’s top surface.
Repeat with a fresh syringe/needle for each different solute.

steps.title: Secure device in enclosure
steps.instruction: Place the filled PDMS‑glass device into the flow‑damping enclosure and fix it with double‑sided scotch tape.

steps.title: Seal enclosure seams
steps.instruction: Tape all seams and holes of the enclosure with scotch tape except the bottom hole; after joining the top and bottom halves, add a vertical tape strip to allow slow water release after deployment.

steps.title: Mount enclosure on deployment arm
steps.instruction: Attach the sealed enclosure to a stable deployment arm using modified wood clamps and secure it with bungy cords.

steps.title: Deploy enclosure in water
steps.instruction: Lower the enclosure into the water, allowing it to fill slowly while venting air; keep the air‑vent (top‑right) as the highest point to ensure all bubbles escape.

steps.title: Plug bottom inlet
steps.instruction: When the enclosure is full, seal the bottom hole with a modified 20 µL pipette tip acting as a plug.

steps.title: Incubate ISCA
steps.instruction: Leave the deployed ISCA in warm water for 1 hour.

steps.title: Retrieve enclosure
steps.instruction: Pull the enclosure out of the water and place it on a level surface.

steps.title: Drain enclosure slowly
steps.instruction: Unseal the enclosure’s drain holes sequentially from top to bottom, allowing the water level to fall to each hole before opening the next; the complete drain should take ~5 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Open the highest drain hole; wait until water level reaches it.
Proceed to the next lower hole, repeating until the enclosure is empty.

steps.title: Recover ISCA from enclosure
steps.instruction: Remove the ISCA, place it on clean Kimwipes to absorb excess water, and use a sterile pipette to remove remaining droplets, drying the device as much as possible.

steps.title: Collect well contents
steps.instruction: Change gloves, then draw the well contents with a 1 mL sterile syringe and 27 G needle (port facing down); pool replicates (≈5 wells per row), fix 80 µL of the pooled volume in 2 % glutaraldehyde (using 25 % stock), and flash‑freeze the remainder in liquid nitrogen for later DNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Attach a 27 G needle to a sterile 1 mL syringe.
Withdraw liquid from each well with the port facing down.
Combine the contents of ~5 wells into one tube.
Add glutaraldehyde to achieve a final 2 % concentration (e.g., add appropriate volume of 25 % stock to 80 µL of sample).
Flash‑freeze the remaining sample in liquid nitrogen.
